chunks: 1761 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:

“Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, disliked for me six traits, and I have disliked them for the awsiya' from my progeny and their followers after me: fidgeting in salat (prayer), obscene speech in sawm (fasting), reminding others of one's charity after giving sadaqah, entering the mosques while junub, peering into houses, and laughing among the graves.”

key_terms.جُنُبًا: in a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.خِصَالٍ: traits or qualities being described as disliked
key_terms.ٱلتَّطَلُّعَ: looking into or peering into others' private spaces
key_terms.ٱلرَّفَثَ: indecent or improper speech during sawm (fasting)
key_terms.ٱلْعَبَثَ: fidgeting or frivolous movement, especially during salat (prayer)
key_terms.ٱلْمَنَّ: reminding others of a favor or charity after giving it

ai.seo_question: What six traits did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم condemn for himself, the awsiya' from his progeny, and their followers?
ai.summary: This hadith lists six blameworthy traits that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, disliked for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and which he also disliked for the awsiya' from his progeny and their followers. It joins matters of worship, ritual purity, charity, privacy, and graveyard etiquette, presenting them as part of the disciplined conduct expected of the Ahl al-Bayt's followers.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1761 - The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said:

"Indeed, Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, has disliked for me six traits, and I also dislike them for the successors from my progeny and their followers after me: carelessness in prayer, inappropriate speech during fasting, reminding others of charity after giving it, entering mosques while in a state of impurity, peering into others' homes, and laughing near graves."
